text: Repeated SSH failed password events may indicate guessing or an incorrectly configured client. Count attempts by source and account over time. Correlate successful logins and subsequent process activity. A few failures alone do not prove compromise.

For SSH hardening, verify a working non-root key-based login and recovery access first. Disable root and password login when appropriate. Use network restrictions and tune Fail2Ban against expected administration. MaxAuthTries is a per-connection limit.

Windows event 4625 is a failed logon and 4624 is a successful logon. Correlate account, source, logon type and time window. Check domain authentication and endpoint activity. A failure alone does not establish malicious intent.

LLMNR and NBT-NS poisoning can redirect authentication toward a rogue host. Inspect name-resolution traffic and unexpected authentication destinations. Disable unneeded fallback protocols after testing DNS dependencies.

SMB signing requirements help mitigate NTLM relay to SMB targets. Verify effective client and server requirements. Other relay targets require separate controls. Reduce legacy NTLM use after auditing compatibility.

WMI remote execution can be legitimate administration or lateral movement. Correlate remote account authentication, WMI activity and child process creation. Review authorized management hosts before classifying the action.

SQL injection arises when untrusted values alter query structure. Use parameterized statements and least-privilege application access. Correlate application errors, HTTP access events and database activity. An HTTP error alone is not proof of exploitation.

An uploaded executable in a web-accessible path can become a web shell. Store uploads outside executable paths, validate content and size, and serve through controlled handlers. Correlate upload requests, file creation and web-server child processes.

Rogue DHCPv6 or related IPv6 name-resolution behavior can redirect domain authentication. Review network protections, WPAD requirements, LDAP signing and LDAPS channel binding. Blanket IPv6 disabling is not a universal hardening baseline.

A scheduled administrator login from an approved management host may be benign. Validate the maintenance window, identity and expected command activity. Even approved accounts can be compromised; investigate contradictory evidence.
